tier_reason: Independent, well-known third party (HAProxy Technologies, W. Tarreau / W. Lallemand) with detailed methodology, gcc-11.4 and AWS r8g.16xlarge Graviton4 (Neoverse V2) stated, comparing AWS-LC against OpenSSL 1.1.1w and 3.0.2-3.4-dev; not A because the test harness/HAProxy configs and optimization flags are not published.

corrections.claimed_speedup: HAProxy 3.1-dev1 on a 64-core Graviton4, at 64 threads (bar charts on page). Full TLS handshake (RSA, new conn/s): AWS-LC v1.32.0+30 commits 63.1k (same with or without the C11 build) vs OpenSSL 1.1.1w 48.3k, OpenSSL 3.1.6-3.4.0-dev 42.6-43.2k, OpenSSL 3.0.2/3.0.14 21.2-21.3k (~1.31x vs 1.1.1w, ~1.46-1.48x vs 3.1+, ~3.0x vs 3.0.x; derived from page data). The older AWS-LC 1.29.0 reached only 45.2k (45.7k with -DCMAKE_C_STANDARD=11), below OpenSSL 1.1.1w, because of a CPU-detection bug. TLS resumption (end-to-end conn/s): AWS-LC 1.29.0 built with -DCMAKE_C_STANDARD=11 186.3k (text: ~183k; v1.32+30-c11 183.7k) with either lock type, vs OpenSSL 1.1.1w 17.8k (pthread locks) / 124.1k (HAProxy locks), OpenSSL 3.1-3.4-dev 23.1-27.9k, OpenSSL 3.0.14 3.7k / 8.1k, OpenSSL 3.0.2 1.6k / 2.3k. The page text says '~20% higher than WolfSSL and 50% higher than OpenSSL 1.1.1w'. The default C99 AWS-LC builds (1.29.0 and 1.32+30) collapsed to 8.4-8.5k with pthread locks and 38.4k with HAProxy locks.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 11.4 (stated on page); AWS-LC's CMake config forced C99 (pthread-rwlock refcounting) unless -DCMAKE_C_STANDARD=11 was set; HAProxy built with and without USE_PTHREAD_EMULATION=1; optimization flags not stated
corrections.workload: HAProxy 3.1-dev1 (2024-06-26) server-only full TLS handshake (RSA, one HTTP request per new connection, no resumption) and end-to-end TLS session resumption from tickets on both the client and backend sides (10 daisy-chained proxy instances), connections/sec vs thread count up to 64, with pthread rwlocks and with HAProxy's lightweight locks (USE_PTHREAD_EMULATION); the TLS protocol version is not stated
corrections.license: Apache-2.0 OR ISC for new AWS-LC code; the LICENSE file lists BoringSSL-derived code as ISC/Apache-2.0, OpenSSL-derived code as Apache-2.0, and bundled parts as MIT, BSD-3-Clause and CC0 (GitHub reports NOASSERTION)
corrections.caveats: Independent third-party benchmark (HAProxy Technologies; tests mid-2024, published 2025-05-06), although AWS supplied HAProxy's AWS-LC patches. The ~63k full-handshake figure is for AWS-LC v1.32.0 plus 30 commits, not 1.29.0; 1.29.0 (~45k) trailed OpenSSL 1.1.1w in that test. Default builds at the time (C99, lock-based refcounting) collapsed in the resumption test to ~8.5k conn/s at 64 threads, worse than OpenSSL 1.1.1w and 3.1+ with pthread locks, until rebuilt with -DCMAKE_C_STANDARD=11 (the page says this was fixed upstream). Only one ARM platform (Graviton4) was tested; gcc 11.4 is stated but optimization flags and the test scripts are not published. Small CC0 parts carry no patent grant.

notes: The record attributed the 63k full-handshake result to AWS-LC 1.29.0-c11 (really 45.7k; 63.1k is v1.32+30). It also gave OpenSSL 3.0.2 ~7-8k in the lightweight-lock resumption test, where the chart shows 2.3k (only 3.0.14 reached 8.1k), and it omitted that the default AWS-LC builds collapsed in resumption. All parts of the LICENSE file are OSI or CC0, so usability changes from mixed to copyable. The AWS-internal usage in stars_or_usage (s2n-tls, SDKs, aws-lc-rs) was not checked.

tier_reason: Independent, well-known third party (HAProxy Technologies) with detailed methodology, gcc-11.4 and AWS r8g.16xlarge Graviton4 stated, comparing wolfSSL 5.7.0 against OpenSSL 1.1.1w and 3.0.2-3.4-dev; not A because the test harness/configs and the wolfSSL build flags are not published.

corrections.claimed_speedup: HAProxy 3.1-dev1 on a 64-core Graviton4, at 64 threads (bar charts on page). Full TLS handshake (RSA, new conn/s): wolfSSL 5.7.0 59.7k (60.6k with HAProxy locks), second only to AWS-LC v1.32+30 (63.1k), vs OpenSSL 1.1.1w 48.3k, OpenSSL 3.1.6-3.4.0-dev 42.6-43.2k, OpenSSL 3.0.2/3.0.14 21.2-21.3k (~1.24x vs 1.1.1w, ~1.38-1.40x vs 3.1+, ~2.8x vs 3.0.x; derived from page data). TLS resumption (end-to-end conn/s): wolfSSL scaled linearly to 149.6k at 64 threads with pthread locks (148.3k with HAProxy locks; text: '150000') vs OpenSSL 1.1.1w 17.8k (pthread) / 124.1k (HAProxy locks), OpenSSL 3.1-3.4-dev 23.1-27.9k, OpenSSL 3.0.14 3.7k ('2.5% of WolfSSL') / 8.1k, and OpenSSL 3.0.2 1.6k ('1500-1600 connections per second ... just 1% of WolfSSL') / 2.3k. AWS-LC 1.29.0 built for C11 was ~20% faster than wolfSSL on resumption.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 11.4 (stated on page for the test builds); wolfSSL configure options and optimization flags not stated (the page notes distro packages lack the build options HAProxy needs and the CPU optimizations, so wolfSSL must be built manually)
corrections.workload: HAProxy 3.1-dev1 (2024-06-26) server-only full TLS handshake (RSA, one HTTP request per new connection, no resumption) and end-to-end TLS session resumption from tickets on both the client and backend sides (10 daisy-chained proxy instances), connections/sec vs thread count up to 64, with pthread rwlocks and with HAProxy's lightweight locks (USE_PTHREAD_EMULATION); the TLS protocol version is not stated
corrections.license: GPL-3.0 (the LICENSING file lets certain listed projects, e.g. MariaDB and OpenVPN, use it under GPL-2.0 instead)
corrections.caveats: Independent third-party benchmark (HAProxy Technologies; tests mid-2024, published 2025-05-06); HAProxy was ported to wolfSSL with help from the wolfSSL team. Distro wolfSSL packages lack the build options HAProxy needs and the CPU optimizations, so a custom build is required, and the OpenSSL-compatibility layer shows occasional behavior differences. Only one ARM platform (Graviton4) was tested; gcc 11.4 is stated but wolfSSL's configure/optimization flags and the test scripts are not published. wolfSSL was not the top performer: AWS-LC v1.32+30 beat it on full handshakes and C11-built AWS-LC beat it by ~20% on resumption. The README separately claims 'dramatically better performance ... over OpenSSL' with no numbers. GPL-3.0 is copyleft.

notes: The record's full-handshake figure was wrong in wolfSSL's disfavor: the chart shows 59.7k/60.6k conn/s, not ~48k (48.3k is OpenSSL 1.1.1w), so wolfSSL beat OpenSSL 1.1.1w by ~24% rather than matching it. The resumption figures (150k vs 17.8k and 1.5-1.6k) match the page. Metadata checks out (GPL-3.0, 2,944 stars, last commit 2026-09-25, not a fork).

tier_reason: First-party NetDev 0x14 (2020) paper by Tempesta Technologies authors. NetDev is a Linux community conference that selects sessions through a call for sessions, not an academic peer-reviewed venue. The paper compares against Nginx 1.19.1/OpenSSL 1.1.1d using public tools (github.com/tempesta-tech/tls-perf, wrk) and names the CPUs (i7-6500U host VM; Xeon E3-1240v5), but compiler, build flags and exact test configs are absent, so it stays at C.

corrections.caveats: This is a first-party paper/benchmark by the Tempesta Technologies team (NetDev 0x14 conference paper, July 2020), not independent peer review, so it is capped at tier C despite the public benchmark tool (tls-perf) and stated hardware; compiler and build flags are not given. The headline 40-80% figure applies mainly to the 1-vCPU VM and to session resumption; the bare-metal new-session gain was only +6%. On bare metal Nginx/OpenSSL had lower average and 95th-percentile latency (the paper says 50-170% lower for new sessions and 4-9% for resumption), and Tempesta showed large tail-latency spikes (max latency up to +3000%, 28,262 vs 925 ms on resumption). The raw ECDSA/ECDHE op/s were lower than OpenSSL even though Tempesta's figures include ephemeral key generation, so that comparison is not like-for-like. Only x86-64 with AVX/BMI/ADX is supported, and the design relies on RDRAND randomization, which SRBDS microcode mitigations slow. Test hardware and kernel (5.7, 2020) are dated, and the code has changed since.

notes: All numbers in claimed_speedup match the paper's tables (2,180 vs 1,545 RPS, 307 vs 1,340 ms, 35,263 vs 19,203, 7,921 vs 7,426, ECDSA 27,261 vs 36,472, ECDHE 6,690 vs 16,619), as do the hardware and baseline versions. The only correction is caveats, which now include the bare-metal latency and tail-latency regressions. The README cites the same 40-80% / x4 claim; the tempesta-tech.com HTTPS-performance KB page has no newer Tempesta numbers (marked TODO). Metadata checks out (GPL-2.0, 722 stars, last commit 2026-09-25 by committer date, not a GitHub fork, though Tempesta TLS began as a fork of mbed TLS 2.8.0).
